text:
jamie: Flagging a cluster of latency spikes hitting p95/p99 for /v1/chat and /v1/generate in hosted-eu-west-1 starting ~15:12 UTC. Reports from several customers and automated alerts. p95 went from ~350ms -> ~1.8s, p99 to ~4.9s.

support-bot: Tickets created: CUST-5002, CUST-5003, CUST-5004. Sample customer says repeated prompt chains slow on retries.

marco: I pulled histogram and traces. Pattern: high cache-miss rate from kv-cache service (redis-cluster) coincident with spikes. Redis server latency spiked to 150-400ms at 15:10-15:20. When cache miss occurs we do a full KV refresh per request which adds ~800ms in tail.

olivia: Any recent infra/config changes touching kv-cache or memory tuning?

infra-bot: config-change detected: runtime-config:prefix_cache_ttl reduced from 300s -> 30s deployed 15:05 UTC via PR #912. Author: marco.

marco: That change was to reduce memory footprint during a test rollout; I rolled it by mistake into prod canary group. It makes prefix cache entries expire faster, inducing more cache rebuilds for repeated prompt families. Combined with a small redis blip, we saw thundering warmups.

jamie: Great find. The trace example:
```
trace: req=xyz789 route=/v1/chat -> router-proxy -> kv-cache-lookup miss 320ms -> fetch-prefix build 760ms -> enqueue GPU exec wait 40ms -> gpu exec 60ms
```

olivia: So most of the extra latency is pre-GPU on the cache/build path. That means batching isn't the culprit here.

jamie: Immediate mitigations (short-term):
1) Revert prefix_cache_ttl to 300s in prod canary and promote.
2) Apply a temporary client-side soft-cache (in proxy) to short-circuit duplicate warmups for identical recent keys for 10s.
3) Add per-customer concurrent request cap (e.g., 50 concurrent small-token requests) to avoid thundering under cache-stress.
4) Use circuit-breaker: if kv-cache_miss_rate_p95 > 20% for 2m then route 20% traffic to fallback model redwood-small-v1 in another region (eu-central-1) and mute heavy retries.

marco: I'll push the revert PR and roll canary -> full within 15m. Command: ```git revert -m 1 PR#912 && deploy runtime-config --env hosted-eu-west-1 --component kv-cache```

ops-bot: Alert: redis-cluster-eu-01 CPU at 94% and cmdlat spikes.

olivia: We should also apply emergency redis protection: enable read-only slave promotion reduction and increase client-side timeouts to avoid cascading retry storms. Ops, can you throttle write-heavy rebuilds?

ops-bot: Initiating redis maintenance mode: reduce eviction pressure by increasing maxmemory-policy to volatile-lru on the cluster nodes, and scaling add-one-node. ETA 12m.

jamie: Early telemetry after canary revert: in the canary region p95 back to ~380ms within 4 minutes. Global p95 trending down. p99 still elevated on eu-west-1 by ~700ms due to remaining redis queue; expect normalization after scaling.

support-bot: Updated tickets: CUST-5002 status=mitigated pending customer confirmation; CUST-5003 status=investigating->mitigated; CUST-5004 status=mitigated. Customer guidance drafted.

olivia: Longer-term mitigations / playbook updates:
- SLO guardrail: disallow decreasing prefix_cache_ttl by >3x in hosted without performance sign-off and a canary smoke test that validates p95/p99 for small token and chained prompts.
- Add a redis-queuebackpressure circuit-breaker: if redis_cmdlat_p95 > 200ms for 1m then automatically lower rebuild concurrency (token_fetch_parallelism) and split traffic to fallback model/region.
- Rate-limit policy: per-account token/sec soft caps for bursty prompt patterns; add a token-bucket fallback that returns 429 with Retry-After header to clients exceeding sustained burst.
- Add a cached-warmup debounce in proxy: group identical prefix warmups within 2s window to a single background job to avoid thundering herd.
- Add deploy gating: any runtime cache policy change must include a perf micro-benchmark that runs 1000 small-token chained prompts in canary and fails the roll if p95 increases >1.25x.

marco: I'll open a follow-up PR with the guardrail policy and modify the deploy pipeline to require the micro-benchmark. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/945

jamie: I'll add a runbook entry under "mitigations -> kv-cache regressions" with explicit commands we used and the circuit-breaker rule IDs. Also: run a customer impact sweep, prioritize customers with highest SLA.

olivia: For the SRE retrospec: collect traces of top 10 affected request IDs, evaluate if we need persistent local LRU in proxies, and model fallback cost trade-offs.

ops-bot: redis cluster scaled +1 node, cmdlat back to normal ~60ms.

jamie: Post-incident checks:
- Confirmed p95 global recovered to ~360-420ms 18 minutes after mitigation.
- p99 dropped below 1.2s in all regions after redis scaling and TTL revert.
- Created action items for redis monitoring, deploy gating, proxy debounce, and rate limiting.

support-bot: Customer notifications queued for CUST-5002/3/4. Template: "We've identified a cache config change causing elevated latency; we've reverted the change and scaled the cache; services are stable; reach out if you see continued issues."

jamie: Closing notes: this was a config-safety failure. Mitigation playbook to add to KB:
- Detect: kv-cache_miss_rate + redis cmdlat alert -> classify as cache-regression.
- Immediate mitigation: revert TTL/config -> scale cache -> enable proxy debounce -> apply temporary per-account concurrency caps -> split traffic to fallback model/region via circuit-breaker.
- Postmortem: add deploy gating + perf canary + SLO rules preventing large cache TTL reductions.

olivia: Thanks all. We'll schedule a retro and mark this Sev2. I'll file the postmortem doc and link here when ready. :heavy_check_mark:
